nodes.label: Phase 0a Exit-Criteria Verification
nodes.rationale: Run from a fresh clone of rust-rewrite at 8bbe1f8 rather than the working tree, so the report describes what a new machine sees. 8 of 8 criteria PASS. CI execution is explicitly out of scope because the branch is deliberately unpushed and the task was told not to push.

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-layers
nodes.rationale: Enforces docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's rule that L2 crates may depend only on L0 and L1, never on each other or on L3. Verified by injecting lapidary-vcs -> lapidary-index, watching it exit 1 naming the edge and the remedy, then reverting to a clean pass over 14 workspace crates.

nodes.label: Prove the Check Bites
nodes.rationale: A check is only verified by deliberately breaking what it guards, confirming a non-zero exit naming that specific problem, then reverting and confirming a clean pass. Asserting that a check passes proves nothing about whether it still checks anything; this repo has repeatedly found checks that silently stopped checking.

nodes.label: Supply-Chain Gate
nodes.rationale: cargo deny check green, both lockfiles committed, and every workflow `uses:` carrying a 40-hex commit SHA. Nine duplicate-crate warnings from sqlx pulling block-buffer/digest at two semver-majors are non-fatal and expected. Whether the workflows execute on GitHub was not verified — that needs a push.

nodes.label: Container Engine Parity
nodes.rationale: The stack builds and serves /api/healthz under both podman and docker, and .containerignore/.dockerignore pairs are byte-identical or the build context is the whole repo. Scope note recorded honestly: rootless podman delegates to the docker-compose CLI plugin, so this exercises two engines but one compose implementation.

nodes.label: Generated-Artifact Staleness Check
nodes.rationale: Regenerate ts-rs bindings and the TanStack route tree in a clean clone with npm ci (never npm install, so no local node_modules interference), then `git diff --exit-code` them. A zero diff is the only proof the checked-in generated files still track the Rust types and the routes.
